subject: Zephyr Health trial — observability readiness & POC checklist
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Mike Sullivan <mike@zephyrhealth.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@zephyrhealth.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Zephyr Health trial — observability readiness & POC checklist

Hi Mike / Sara,

Thanks again for the call today — great context on your evaluation goals. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the proposed trial scope, success criteria, and concrete next steps so we can align owners and get the POC started next week. I’ve attached a one-pager scope and an observability template you can review.

Summary / Scope (30d trial, dev -> staging):
- Target workload: 10k inference calls/day, mixed chat+batch embedding jobs.
- Data residency: US-only. No PHI will be sent in trial inputs (Zephyr confirmed).
- Models: rwd-medium and rwd-quant-fast variants for latency/cost comparison.

Top success criteria (agreed on call):
1) Latency SLA: 95th percentile generation latency <= 350ms for typical chat requests (<= 1024 tokens).
2) Cost delta: Per-1000-token cost using rwd-quant-fast <= 60% of baseline.
3) Functional parity: sample prompt set (attached) yields acceptable fidelity — fewer than 3 regressions flagged by your SME set.
4) Reliability: sustained availability >= 99.5% during test windows.

Observability plan (what we will deliver / what we need from you):
- Dashboards: latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), tokens per request, error rate by model/version, request volume by route. Redwood will populate a Grafana dashboard in the shared Drive.
- Tracing: end-to-end traces for representative flows (frontend -> Redwood -> backend). We’ll instrument with distributed trace IDs — need an example request flow from your engineering team.
- Logs: request/response metadata export (no full text bodies) to your logging endpoint (s3/loki). We will provide a log schema; you confirm acceptable fields.
- Metrics to monitor: request_count, inference_duration_ms, decode_token_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate, oom_count, model_fallback_count.

Ownership & timeline:
- This week (Nov 23–27): Redwood to provision trial cluster + observability dashboards; Zephyr to whitelist IPs and share sample traffic and SME prompt set.
- Next week (Nov 30–Dec 4): smoke tests and baseline run with 1–2k/day; iterate on dashboard thresholds.
- Week of Dec 7: full workload run and evaluation window.

Action items (owners):
- Redwood (Vanessa): deliver dashboard links + config, start cluster provisioning (ETA Nov 25).
- Redwood (Sergio): prepare tracing hooks and log export connector; will share schema by EOD Nov 23.
- Zephyr (Mike/Sara): provide sample request flows, confirm log sink, and share SME prompt set by Nov 25.
- Zephyr (procurement): we’ll coordinate a simple MSA + trial SOW; procurement contact copied for expectations.

Attachments: zephyr_poc_scope.xlsx (scope + milestones), redwood_observability_templates.pdf (dashboard + metric templates).

If that aligns, I’ll create the HubSpot milestone and schedule a working session with Sergio and your infra lead on Nov 24.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0184

Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference for production
From: Mike Sullivan <mike@zephyrhealth.com>

Cc: procurement@zephyrhealth.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Zephyr Health trial — observability readiness & POC checklist

Thanks Vanessa — this looks good and matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We can provide a sanitized sample of representative traffic by Nov 25. It will be routed from our staging cluster; I’ll include the network team in the working session.
- On logging, we prefer S3 export (log objects) with the schema you propose — confirm compression and rotation settings in your schema doc.
- Metrics: we’d also like per-customer labels (customer_id) for the trial runs so our product analytics can map to feature teams. Is that acceptable?

Procurement note (cc): we’ll aim to finalize the trial SOW and low-risk MSA this week. If Redwood can provide a short SOW addendum that limits data types (no PHI) and scope, that would speed procurement.

Can you lock in the Nov 24 working session at 11am PT? That time works for our infra lead.

— Mike
VP Product, Zephyr Health
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Zephyr Health trial — observability readiness & POC checklist

Vanessa / Lauren —

I’ll own the tracing + log export work. Plan:
- Today (Nov 24): publish trace instrumentation guide (X-Ray-compatible header) and log schema to the shared Drive.
- Nov 25: create Grafana dashboard (latency / token metrics) and wire up to the trial cluster metrics endpoint.
- Nov 29: run an internal smoke trace with sample traffic and verify S3 export.

Questions for Zephyr (to ask in working session):
1) Which S3 bucket/account will receive logs? Any encryption/KMS constraints?
2) Do you want full request IDs surfaced to traces or just anonymized IDs?
3) Any additional alerting thresholds beyond p95 latency and error_rate > 0.5%?

I’ll attach the initial dashboard JSON to the Drive and post the link in the HubSpot activity once ready.

— Sergio
